How to read Diagnostic and Synthesis results

Monderman has four diagnostics: Structural Clarity, Decision Velocity, Operational Systems, and Institutional Performance. One run produces an individual report. The four lens examples here go a step further: each compares responses from 15 people in an organization with 30 eligible participants. They show differences in experience and practical next steps while more responses are collected. These examples are not yet eligible for Depth Synthesis and do not present organizational savings.

Depth Synthesis examines responses to one diagnostic once the campaign meets its evidence requirements. Cross-Lens Synthesis brings eligible results from multiple diagnostics together, keeping differences visible. One person is counted once within each lens and once across the campaign, even if they complete all four diagnostics. The Workspace shows what is ready and what is still needed. The Synthesis examples include separate operating records and change assumptions to estimate time, spending and capacity benefits. Staff capacity is time available for other work, not automatically cash savings.

How to read Diagnostic and Synthesis results

Monderman has four diagnostics: Structural Clarity, Decision Velocity, Operational Systems, and Institutional Performance. An individual report explains one participant’s result, the conditions their responses describe, and practical next steps. Supporting answers and evidence remain visible alongside the findings. A single run does not estimate organizational exposure, recovery or ROI; any recorded time answer remains one participant’s report.

One participant may complete several Diagnostics, but those responses do not become several independent participants. Depth Synthesis compares eligible included responses to the same diagnostic within a defined scope. Cross-Lens Synthesis brings multiple diagnostics together while keeping each result visible. A combined score appears only when the inputs meet Monderman’s comparison requirements; otherwise, the report explains why the scores remain separate. The Workspace explains whether the selected inputs meet the requirements for each Synthesis. Separate cost scenarios require operational measurements, change and adoption assumptions, and explicit costs; capacity value is not cash savings.
